ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the diagonals AC and BD of the rhombus ABCD intersect at point O, and point E is the midpoint of side AB. If $OE = 6$, what is the length of BC?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, \\
it follows that $OA=OC$, \\
since point E is the midpoint of side AB, \\
it follows that $OE$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$, \\
hence $BC=2OE=2\times 6=\boxed{12}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, quadrilateral ABCD is drawn in the shape of a rhombus, with A on the left, C on the right, D above, and B below; diagonals AC and BD intersect at an interior point O; point E is marked on side AB, and there is segment OE in the figure. The problem text states that ABCD is a rhombus, E is the midpoint of AB, and OE=6. Reasoning: Because a rhombus is a parallelogram, its diagonals bisect each other, so O is the midpoint of AC. In triangle ABC, E is the midpoint of AB, and O is the midpoint of AC, so OE is the midline of triangle ABC. The length of the midline is equal to half of the third side BC, that is, OE=BC/2. Given OE=6, so BC=2×6=12.
